    AI Overview
    The Artemis II crewed moon rocket launch is scheduled for Wednesday, April 1, 2026, with a launch window opening at 6:24 p.m. EDT, available to watch on
    NASA's YouTube channel, NASA+, and NBC News NOW. Live coverage also includes CBS News 24/7 and FOX Weather's YouTube channel. 
    Where to Watch the Artemis II Launch (April 1, 2026): 
    • Online/Streaming:
      • NASA YouTube: Official coverage starting at 12:50 p.m. EDT.
      • NASA+: NASA's streaming service.
      • NBC News NOW: Coverage starts before 6:24 p.m. EDT.
      • CBS News 24/7: Coverage starts at 4 p.m. EDT.
      • FOX Weather: Live stream available on YouTube.
    • TV/Apps:
      • CBS News: Local CBS stations.
      • Smart TV Apps: Available via Amazon Prime, Apple TV, Hulu, Netflix, and Roku. 
    The mission will send four astronauts (Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen) around the moon, marking a significant milestone for NASA. If the launch is delayed, backup dates are available through early April.
